messages.author: 1c31a8eb2c5ca537
messages.subject: Timezone and start_time
parts:
Dear Vincent,

Thank you for developing this very useful R package! I am using it (ver 1.5-12) to extract variables from geneactiv data but I am having this problem.
 
I ran part 1 and 2 of the package and I set the timezone as Europe/Amsterdam (desirestz="Europe/Amsterdam"). However, looking at the part 2 summary and meta data it seems that the start_time and the first timestamp are not correct. The start_time (and the first timestamp) is always 18:15, but the data collection started at 19:00 in Europe/Amsterdam timezone.

I ran again part 1 and 2 on a couple of files without changing the timezone but I obtained the same start_time (18:15).

I hope you could help me with it.

Kind regards,

Sonia

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Timezone and start_time
parts:
Hi Sonia,

It probably interprets the start time as 18:00 and as is the default in GGIR looks for the next integer number of 15 minutes in an hour to start reporting results. The 15 minute setting is modifiable.

Why the start time is interpreted as 18:00 and not as 19:00 may depend on accelerometer brand and computer on which the sensor was initialised. I would need more information to answer your question.

General comment to all - please try to post your tech issues in the github: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues. This email list is mainly for questions relevant to all GGIR users.

Thanks
